name: Nuragic civilisation
title: The story of the Nuragic civilisation

text: About 3,800 years ago, people on Sardinia began to build stone towers called nuraghi.
Chiefs lived in the biggest towers, and others lived nearby in round stone houses.
src: The Nuragic people of Sardinia built the nuraghe, a stone tower with vaulted inner chambers, in large numbers from about 1800 BCE / c. 1800–1600 BCE: The first proto-nuraghi are built
each led by a chief who lived in a complex nuraghe, while ordinary people lived in nearby villages of stone roundhouses with straw roofs

text: Water was at the heart of their religion, and they built holy wells over sacred springs.
src: Water stood at the centre of worship. The holy wells, built like the nuraghi with a vaulted round chamber reached by a monumental stair, gathered the water of sacred springs

text: Their metalworkers cast small bronze statues of chiefs, warriors, musicians, animals and ships.
Sardinia was rich in copper, and its people became some of Europe’s main metal makers.
src: Bronze statuettes show chief-kings with cloaks and staffs, and miners, artisans, musicians, wrestlers and many warriors / showing scenes of everyday life, people of different ranks, animals, gods and ships
Sardinia was rich in copper and lead, and the Nuragic people became among the main metal producers of Europe

text: Bronze needs tin, which Sardinia hardly had, so they traded for it.
Their pottery and bronzes travelled by sea to the Aegean, Cyprus, Spain and Italy.
src: Bronze needed tin, which the island hardly had, so they had to trade for it
their pottery and bronzes reached the Aegean, Cyprus, Spain and the Etruscan cities of Italy

text: Later, Carthage took the coasts, and then Rome took the whole island.
Nuragic ways lasted long in the mountains, and more than 7,000 towers still dot Sardinia.
src: Carthage took the coasts in the 6th century BCE and Rome the island in 238 BCE
but Nuragic ways lasted long in the mountainous interior / More than 7,000 nuraghi still dot Sardinia
